prompt: An ideal pulse spends one third of each cycle high. A harmonic vanishes when a whole number of its cycles fits inside that high interval. Which pattern of missing harmonics follows?

options.explanation: That is the half-cycle duty case: a square wave.
Correct. The sine of π times n/3 is zero whenever n is a multiple of 3.

options.text: None; only a square wave has missing harmonics
options.explanation: Any width that is a simple fraction makes some harmonics vanish.
The fundamental is never zero for widths between 0 and 1; here its sine factor is about 0.87.

workedExample: The third harmonic completes one cycle during the high third of the fundamental period. The sixth completes two and the ninth three, so the cancellation repeats every third harmonic. Changing duty fraction moves this missing-harmonic pattern and changes timbre.
